# port-control-wsl

> From inside WSL2 (Linux): pass USB devices through to WSL with usbipd, and
> drive serial consoles on embedded devices (SBCs, dev boards, routers) over
> /dev/ttyUSB* — list COM ports, send commands, stream output, log in, run
> shells. A general COM-port remote shell (SSH-style over serial). Aimed at
> embedded development from WSL2.

Keywords: WSL, WSL2, usbipd, USB passthrough, USB/IP, serial port, serial
console, COM port, /dev/ttyUSB0, ttyUSB, FTDI, CH340, CP210x, pyserial, UART,
embedded, SBC, dev board, router, U-Boot, BusyBox, Windows, DTR, RTS,
Linux-to-Windows.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): Overview, requirements, full command list (USB + serial), configuration, DTR/RTS note, security notes.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Machine-readable guide for AI agents — exact commands, deps, preconditions, safety.

## Code

- [port_control.py](port_control.py): The whole tool. CLI subcommands: `usb-list`, `usb-attach`, `usb-detach`, `serial-list`, `serial-send`, `serial-read`, `serial-login`, `serial-shell`.
- [requirements.txt](requirements.txt): `pyserial` (serial commands only).

## Dependencies

- pyserial — for the serial-* commands (not needed for usb-*).
- usbipd-win (https://github.com/dorssel/usbipd-win) — for USB passthrough on Windows.
- [wsl-win-admin-bridge](https://github.com/marcus-lhkmarcus/wsl-win-admin-bridge): provides `win_admin.py`, used for the elevated `usbipd bind` in usb-attach/usb-detach. Loaded lazily; set `WIN_ADMIN` to its path. usb-list and serial commands don't need it.

## Quick start

- `pip install -r requirements.txt`
- `python3 port_control.py usb-list` → find the bus ID
- `python3 port_control.py usb-attach 6-3` → attach to WSL
- `python3 port_control.py serial-shell /dev/ttyUSB0 --user root --cmd "uname -a"`

## Notes

- `_get_serial()` clears DTR/RTS after open — some FTDI dev cables corrupt the device UART otherwise.
- Default baud 115200; serial helpers tuned for BusyBox-style embedded consoles.
- Device-specific actions (reboot, kill/start a process) are ordinary `serial-shell` commands — no per-device subcommands.
